q: We had to ___ the picnic because of the storm.
explain: Call off = cancel. Example: The match was called off.

notes.put up: Put up = build or let someone stay.
notes.take off: Take off = remove clothes, or a plane leaving.

q: The fox was ___ to find its way out of the maze.
explain: Unable to + verb = can't. Example: I was unable to sleep.

notes.impossible: Impossible describes the task, not the fox.

q: I can't ___ up with this noise any longer!
explain: Put up with = accept something annoying. Example: I can't put up with the cold.

notes.keep: Keep up with = go at the same speed.
notes.make: Make up = invent or become friends again.

q: Can you ___ after my plants while I'm away?
explain: Look after = take care of. Example: She looks after her little brother.

notes.take: Take care needs 'of': take care of.
notes.care: Care for means love or nurse, not 'care after'.

q: The journey took longer than we ___.
explain: Expect = think something will happen. Example: It was easier than I expected.

q: She ___ a promise to return before sunset.
explain: We make a promise. Example: He made a promise to help.

q: The castle guard was very ___; he never let anyone break the rules.
explain: Strict = makes people follow rules. Example: Our teacher is strict about homework.

notes.generous: Generous means kind with money or gifts.
notes.relaxed: Relaxed is the opposite of strict.

q: We need to ___ a decision soon.
explain: We make a decision. Example: It's hard to make decisions.

q: I'm really ___ forward to the festival.
explain: Look forward to = be happy about something coming. Example: I look forward to seeing you.

q: The old bridge is ___ — please don't cross it.
explain: After is we need an adjective: dangerous. Example: That road is dangerous.

notes.dangerously: Dangerously is an adverb: drive dangerously.
notes.endangered: Endangered is for animals at risk of dying out.

q: Which word means the same as 'enormous'?
explain: Enormous = huge = very big. Example: a huge whale.

q: The wizard's ___ was that it would rain for a week.
explain: A prediction says what will happen. Example: The weather prediction was right.

notes.prescription: A prescription is from a doctor.

q: Could you ___ me how to get to the lake?
explain: Tell + person + how. Example: Tell me your name.

notes.explain: Explain needs 'to': explain to me how.

q: He ___ the bus, so he walked to the village.
explain: Miss = be too late for transport. Example: I missed the train.

notes.lost: Lose is for things you can't find.

q: That song ___ me of my summer holidays.
explain: Remind someone of = make them think of. Example: You remind me of my sister.

q: We've run ___ of milk. Can you buy some?
explain: Run out of = have none left. Example: We ran out of time.

notes.down: Run down = lose power or criticise.

q: Could you ___ down the music? I'm trying to study.
explain: Turn down = make quieter. Example: Turn down the TV.

notes.put: Put down = place on a surface.
notes.get: Get down = come down or make sad.

q: The festival was a great ___; thousands of people came.
explain: A success = something that goes well. Example: The party was a success.

notes.victory: A victory is for a battle or game.

q: I ___ my dad; we both love painting.
explain: Take after = be like an older family member. Example: She takes after her mum.

q: The hotel room was ___: clean, quiet and with a lake view.
explain: Comfortable = nice to be in. Example: a comfortable bed.

notes.comforting: Comforting means making you feel less sad.
notes.comfort: Comfort is a noun or verb.

q: Let's ___ a break — we've been walking for hours.
explain: Take a break = rest. Example: Let's take a break.

notes.get: Get a break means a lucky chance.

q: She's very ___; she always tells the truth.
explain: Honest = tells the truth. Example: an honest answer.

q: The price ___ breakfast and dinner.
explain: Include = have as part of the whole. Example: The ticket includes a drink.

notes.contains: Contain is for what's inside a container.
notes.involves: Involve means take part or need.

q: I ___ to get the job, but I'm going to keep trying.
explain: Fail to = not succeed. Example: He failed to reach the top.

notes.refused: Refuse means say no on purpose.

q: Please ___ in mind that the gates close at six.
explain: Bear in mind = remember. Example: Bear in mind it might rain.

notes.take: Take in mind isn't the phrase.
notes.hold: Hold in mind isn't the phrase.
notes.have: Have in mind means plan or think of.

q: The road was ___ because of the flood.
explain: Blocked = nobody can pass. Example: A tree blocked the road.

q: He ___ his ankle while playing football.
explain: Twist your ankle = hurt it by turning it. Example: I twisted my ankle on the stairs.

notes.damaged: Damage is for things, not body parts.
notes.hurt himself: Hurt himself can't be followed by 'his ankle'.

q: Which word means 'very tired'?
explain: Exhausted = very, very tired. Example: I was exhausted after the race.

q: We set ___ early to avoid the traffic.
explain: Set off = start a journey. Example: We set off at dawn.

notes.up: Set up = start a business or prepare.
notes.in: Set in = begin and continue (bad weather).

q: She ___ an effort to talk to everyone at the party.
explain: Make an effort = try hard. Example: Make an effort to listen.

q: The fire alarm ___ during the maths test.
explain: Go off = an alarm starts ringing (or a bomb explodes).

notes.went out: Go out = stop burning, or leave home.

q: Our teacher ___ the class into four teams.
explain: Split up = divide into groups.

notes.split off: Split off isn't used for teams here.

q: Let's ___ a lemonade stall on Saturday.
explain: Set up = start or prepare something.

q: I've decided to ___ chess. My grandpa will teach me.
explain: Take up = start a new hobby.

notes.take off: Take off = remove, or a plane leaving.
notes.take after: Take after = look like a family member.

q: The match was ___ until next week because of rain.
explain: Put off = postpone.

notes.put up: Put up = build or let someone stay.
notes.put on: Put on = wear, or start a show.

q: The firefighters ___ the fire quickly.
explain: Put out a fire = make it stop burning.

notes.put away: Put away = tidy into its place.
notes.put down: Put down = place on a surface.

q: Please ___ your books now. The lesson is over.
explain: Put away = put back in its place.

notes.put through: Put through = connect on the phone.

q: I ___ an old friend at the park yesterday.
explain: Run into = meet by chance.

notes.ran over: Run over = hit with a vehicle.

q: We've ___ glue. Can you get some more?
explain: Run out of = have none left.

notes.run over: Run over = hit with a vehicle.

q: The plan didn't ___. We had to try something else.
explain: Work out = succeed, have a good result.

notes.work off: Work off = get rid of by exercise.

q: I ___ well with my cousin. We're best friends.
explain: Get on (well) with = have a good relationship.

q: It took me a week to ___ my cold.
explain: Get over = recover from an illness or sad event.

notes.get on: Get on = have a good relationship.
notes.get through to: Get through to = reach on the phone.

q: Can you ___ the meaning of this word for me?
explain: Look up a word = find it in a dictionary.

q: ___! There's a bike coming!
explain: Look out! = be careful.

notes.Look up: Look up = find in a dictionary.

q: I ___ my coat because it was getting cold.
explain: Put on = start wearing.

notes.got on: Get on = board a bus or train.

q: She ___ the invitation because she was busy.
explain: Turn down an invitation = say no to it.

q: Only five people ___ for the club meeting.
explain: Turn up = arrive, appear.

q: The caterpillar ___ a butterfly.
explain: Turn into = become.

q: The baby ___ her mum. They have the same smile.
explain: Take after = look or act like an older relative.

q: You have to ___ attention in class.
explain: Collocation: pay attention.

notes.give: We don't say give attention here.

q: I ___ a mistake in my spelling.
explain: Collocation: make a mistake.

notes.did: We don't say do a mistake.
notes.took: We don't say take a mistake.

q: Can you ___ me a favour and hold this?
explain: Collocation: do someone a favour.

notes.make: We don't say make a favour.

q: We need to ___ a decision before Friday.
explain: Come to / make / reach a decision.

notes.do: We don't say do a decision.
notes.get to: Get to a decision isn't usual.
notes.go to: Go to a decision isn't English.

q: Please ___ care when you cross the road.
explain: Collocation: take care.

q: Our team ___ the match 3–1.
explain: You win a match/game; you beat a team.

notes.beat: Beat needs a team: we beat them.

q: We ___ the other team 3–1.
explain: Beat + opponent; win + game.

q: I'm saving up to ___ a new skateboard.
explain: Afford = have enough money for.

notes.lend: Lend = give for a short time.

q: I ___ my brother £2. I'll pay him back tomorrow.
explain: Owe = have to pay back.

notes.borrow: Borrow needs from: borrow from him.

q: Can I ___ your ruler? I'll give it back.
explain: Borrow = take for a short time; lend = give for a short time.

notes.lend: Lend is what the owner does.
notes.loan you: Loan you would mean giving your ruler away.

q: She ___ pocket money by washing the car.
explain: Earn money for work.

notes.wins: Win is for prizes and games.
notes.gains: Gain is for weight or experience.

q: The ___ was hard. I only got half the questions.
explain: An exam is a test.

notes.exercise book: An exercise book is for writing in.
notes.examiner: An examiner is the person who checks it.
notes.excuse: An excuse is a reason you give.

q: I ___ my homework at home!
explain: Leave something somewhere = not bring it.

notes.forgot: Forget doesn't take a place: I forgot my homework.
notes.missed: Miss is for buses or people.

q: Please ___ quiet in the library.
explain: Keep quiet = stay silent.

notes.hold: Hold is for things in your hand.
notes.stay to: Stay quiet works, but not stay to.

q: The movie was ___. Everyone cried at the end.
explain: -ing adjective: something is moving (makes you feel emotion).

notes.moved: Moved is how the people felt.

q: I was ___ by the magic show!
explain: -ed = how you feel.

q: The ___ of the race was a girl from my class.
explain: Word family: win → winner (person).

q: Thanks for your ___. It really helped.
explain: Advice (noun, uncountable); advise (verb).

q: Could you ___ me which book to read?
explain: Advise someone (verb).

notes.recommend me: Recommend me isn't the right pattern here.

q: I need some ___ about the school trip.
explain: Information is uncountable.

q: The ___ in the park was beautiful.
explain: Scenery is uncountable.

q: I ___ a lot about volcanoes from that video.
explain: Learn = get knowledge; teach = give it.

notes.taught: Teach is what the video does to you.
notes.knew: Knew doesn't show getting new knowledge.

q: Mr Tan ___ us how to make paper boats.
explain: Teach → taught.

q: Can you ___ me up at 7?
explain: Wake someone up.

q: Please ___ your hand if you know the answer.
explain: Raise + object; rise has no object.

notes.rise: Rise has no object: the sun rises.

q: The sun ___ in the east.
explain: Rise (no object).

notes.rose up it: Rose is past and 'up it' is wrong.

q: Please be ___ with that vase. It's old.
explain: Adjective after be: careful.

q: It was ___ of you to leave the door open.
explain: Careless = not careful.

q: That's ___! A cat can't drive a bus.
explain: Opposite prefix: im- before p.

q: I ___ with you. I think it's a great idea.
explain: Agree with someone.

q: It's ___ to talk with your mouth full.
explain: Polite → impolite.

q: The ___ of the bridge took two years.
explain: Verb → noun with -ion.

q: We need more ___ for the school garden.
explain: A volunteer = a person who helps for free.

q: He's a very ___ dancer.
explain: Talent (noun) → talented (adjective).

q: I'm ___ forward to the holidays.
explain: Look forward to = be excited about.

q: The ___ was full of colourful fish.
explain: An aquarium has fish tanks.

q: We ___ plastic bottles to help the planet.
explain: Recycle = make used things into new things.

notes.reuse once: Reuse once isn't a set phrase.

q: Turn off the lights to save ___.
explain: Save energy = use less electricity.

notes.power cut: A power cut is when electricity stops.
notes.battery life: Battery life is for a device.

q: Too much rubbish causes ___ in the sea.
explain: Pollution (noun).

notes.polluter: A polluter is a person or company.

q: Pandas are an ___ species. There are very few left.
explain: Endangered = in danger of disappearing.

notes.dangerous: Dangerous means it can hurt you.

q: Dinosaurs are ___. There are none left.
explain: Extinct = no longer exist.

q: I need to ___ my phone. The battery is low.
explain: Charge a battery.

notes.plug: Plug needs in: plug it in.

q: Don't forget to ___ your work before you close the file.
explain: Save a file.

q: I typed my ___ wrong, so I couldn't log in.
explain: A password lets you log in.

q: The ___ blew the whistle at the end of the match.
explain: The referee controls the match.

q: Our ___ makes us run ten laps every practice.
explain: A coach trains a team.

q: Thousands of ___ watched the final.
explain: Spectators = people who watch.

notes.referees: There are only a few referees.

q: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres.
explain: Break a record = do better than the record.

notes.made out: Make out means see with difficulty.

q: I can't ___ which colour to choose.
explain: Can't + base verb: decide.

q: Let's have a ___ about our class project.
explain: Discussion (noun) after a.

q: I ___ my little sister to do her puzzle.
explain: Encourage someone to do something = give them confidence.

q: It took a lot of ___ to sing on stage.
explain: Courage = bravery (noun).

q: My brother is ___ of spiders. He runs away!
explain: Terrified = very scared.

q: The roller coaster was ___!
explain: -ing adjective describes the ride.

q: We had to ___ for an hour to see the koalas.
explain: Queue = wait in a line (British).

notes.cue: Cue is a signal (sounds the same!).

q: The museum has an ___ about space.
explain: Exhibition = a public show of things.

q: They went on an ___ to the North Pole.
explain: Expedition = a long journey with a purpose.

notes.experience: Experience is something you live through.

q: I'm ___ to peanuts. I can't eat them.
explain: Allergic to = your body reacts badly.

q: My cut is ___ better.
explain: Get + comparative = become.

notes.turning to: Turn to isn't used with better.

q: The test was ___ easier than I expected.
explain: Much + comparative.

q: I've ___ finished my book. Just one page left!
explain: Nearly = almost.

q: I ___ forgot my lines in the play, but I remembered just in time!
explain: Almost = nearly.

notes.at most: At most means not more than.

q: There was a ___ of the new film in the newspaper.
explain: A review gives an opinion about a film or book.

notes.view: A view is what you see.

q: I'm doing ___ for my exams.
explain: British English: do revision = study for exams.

q: The ___ to the castle costs £5.
explain: Entrance fee = money to go in.

notes.entry way: An entry way is a door.
notes.ticket office: A ticket office is where you pay.

q: Please write your ___ here so we can post the prize.
explain: Address: two d's, two s's.

q: I ___ my mum with the cooking.
explain: Help someone with something.

q: Could you ___ the dishes, please?
explain: Could you + base verb?

q: I'd like to ___ a complaint. My pizza is cold!
explain: Collocation: make a complaint.

notes.do: We don't say do a complaint.

q: She ___ her best friend's secret. Now they aren't talking.
explain: Give away a secret = tell it by accident or on purpose.

notes.gave in: Give in = stop arguing and agree.

q: After hours of begging, Dad finally ___ and let us get a puppy.
explain: Give in = finally agree after saying no.

notes.gave away: Give away = tell a secret or give for free.
notes.gave out: Give out = hand to many people.
notes.gave off: Give off = send out a smell or heat.

q: The teacher ___ the worksheets to everyone.
explain: Hand out = give to each person.

notes.handed in: Hand in = give your work to the teacher.
notes.handed over to: Handed over to needs a person after it.
notes.handed down: Hand down = pass to younger family.

q: Please ___ your homework by Friday.
explain: Hand in = give your work to the teacher.

notes.hand down: Hand down = pass to the next generation.
notes.hand on: Hand on isn't used for homework.

q: Spell the word: a person who writes books
explain: An author writes books.

q: Spell the word: to say no to an invitation politely
explain: If you decline an invitation, you say no politely.

q: Spell the word: a word that means the same as another word
explain: Big and large are synonyms.

q: Spell the word: very surprised
explain: We were amazed by the magician's trick.

q: Spell the word: to make something bigger
explain: The school will expand and add five new classrooms.

q: Spell the word: the opposite of ancient
explain: Ancient = very old; modern = new and up to date.

q: Spell the word: a list of things you must do or buy
explain: Tick each item on your checklist.

q: Spell the word: a person who saw something happen
explain: A witness saw what happened.

q: Spell the word: to find something for the first time
explain: Scientists discover new animals every year.

q: Spell the word: a small mistake in spelling or typing
explain: A typo is a small typing mistake.

q: Spell the word: feeling worried before something important
explain: I was nervous before my piano exam.

q: Spell the word: to go back to a place again
explain: We will return to the beach next summer.

q: Spell the word: the people who watch a show
explain: The audience clapped at the end of the play.

q: Spell the word: an animal that hunts other animals
explain: A fox is a predator; it hunts rabbits.

q: Spell the word: water falling from the sky in small pieces of ice
explain: Hail is little balls of ice falling from the sky.

q: Spell the word: a journey on a ship for fun
explain: They went on a cruise around the islands.

q: Spell the word: to keep something safe from harm
explain: Helmets protect your head.

q: Spell the word: not easy to break
explain: This rope is strong; it won't break.

q: Spell the word: the place where you show your passport when you travel
explain: We showed our passports at the border.

q: Spell the word: a short film that advertises something
explain: That advert for trainers is really funny.

q: Spell the word: to say sorry
explain: He apologised for breaking the vase.

q: Spell the word: a person who goes to a shop to buy things
explain: The shop was full of customers.

q: Spell the word: feeling sure you can do something well
explain: She feels confident about her speech.

q: Spell the word: to pick fruit or crops when they are ready
explain: Farmers harvest apples in autumn.

q: Spell the word: the noise a crowd makes when it is happy
explain: The fans gave a big cheer.

q: Spell the word: the money you get for doing a job
explain: A salary is the money you earn at work.

q: Spell the word: a place where scientists do experiments
explain: Scientists test ideas in a laboratory.

q: Spell the word: not the same; different from all others
explain: Every snowflake is unique.

q: Spell the word: to make a guess about the future
explain: Can you predict who will win?

q: Spell the word: a very old object from the past
explain: This clock is an antique; it is 200 years old.

q: Spell the word: to put money away to use later
explain: I save my pocket money for a new bike.

q: Spell the word: a person who is learning a job
explain: The trainee chef is learning from the head chef.

q: Spell the word: to get better after being ill
explain: It took a week to recover from the flu.

q: Spell the word: tired of doing the same thing
explain: I was bored in the long car journey.

q: Spell the word: a group of musicians who play together
explain: My cousin plays drums in a band.

q: Spell the word: to stop something from happening
explain: Brushing your teeth helps prevent holes.

q: Spell the word: an area of very dry land with little rain
explain: Camels live in the desert.

q: Spell the word: a sudden very strong feeling of fear
explain: Don't panic; stay calm and walk out.

q: Spell the word: to share out cards or jobs between people
explain: Let's divide the jobs between us.

q: Spell the word: a person who visits a place on holiday
explain: Lots of tourists visit the castle in summer.

q: Spell the word: a person you compete against
explain: My opponent in the chess final was very good.
